articles.title: A qué hora es el Real Sociedad - Olympique Lyon hoy: horario y dónde ver en TV el partido de Europa League
articles.standfirst: Te contamos dónde seguir en directo el partido de la jornada 4 de la Europa League
articles.summary: Te contamos dónde seguir en directo el partido de la jornada 4 de la Europa League
articles.body: El conjunto donostiarra quiere olvidar el tropiezo en el derbi vasco frente al Athletic Club reconquistando la Europa League a costa de un Olympique de Lyon descabezado por la marcha repentina de Paulo Fonseca, que deja al banquillo galo en manos de un preparador interino. Con la moral intacta tras el contundente 0-6 endosado al Lillestrøm en la última cita continental, la escuadra dirigida por Pellegrino Matarazzo aspira a meterse de lleno en la zona noble del top-8, aprovechando la debilidad de unos franceses que apenas aventajan en dos unidades a los blanquiazules. La Real, quinta en la Liga tras ver cortada su excelente dinámica de cuatro triunfos ligueros consecutivos, busca hacer valer su condición de local en Europa, donde actualmente ocupa la decimocuarta posición con un balance equilibrado de un triunfo, unas tablas y una derrota. Anoeta acogerá este jueves, 5 de noviembre de 2026, a partir de las 18:45 horas, el encuentro de la fase de liga de la Europa League que enfrentará a la Real Sociedad y al Olympique de Lyon. El encuentro de la Europa League entre el conjunto donostiarra y el Olympique de Lyon se retransmitirá en directo por televisión a través de M+ Liga de Campeones. El encuentro podrá seguirse también a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde varias horas antes del inicio se podrán consultar la última hora de ambos equipos, las alineaciones probables y todas las novedades de una cita clave para las aspiraciones europeas de la Real. Tras el partido, estarán disponibles la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas, el análisis y el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles.

articles.title: The secret behind Miami's explosive offense? A Louisiana country boy who almost walked away from football
articles.summary: Shannon Dawson nearly quit coaching seven years ago to return to the Louisiana backwoods. Now, he's married Air Raid concepts with Mario Cristobal's bruising...
articles.body:
CORAL GABLES, Fla. — The wallpaper of Shannon Dawson's office is a tapestry of a football coach's first language: Xs and Os.

Scribbled in black marker, scrawled across three of four walls in the Miami offensive coordinator's digs are play designs, route concepts and offensive formations. You can barely make them out. A film junkie, Dawson's office is often dimly lit as a television glows from across the room.

But as the lights flicker on, the walls come alive. There's a surprise here too: a fourth wall — a window looking out to the team's indoor practice facility — is also covered in play designs.

Window or wall, no surface can escape Dawson's felted weapon.

"We call it 'The Think Tank,'" Dawson says of the window, which, unlike the three walls, holds concepts to be used at a later date instead of the current game week.

A country boy at heart, his accent dripping with those south Louisiana and Mississippi roots, the 49-year-old Dawson helps steer the nation's most explosive offense for the country's top-ranked team.

Miami deploys college football's most efficient and productive quarterback (Darian Mensah completes 80% of his passes and throws for the sixth-most yards in the sport); its most electrifying receiver (Malachi Toney has caught the second-most touchdowns); and two bruising backs (Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory combine for 16 scores).

As the unbeaten Hurricanes barrel toward perhaps the most anticipated regular game in college football this year — No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend — Dawson's unit is humming at a breakneck pace: no team averages more points a game (46.7); no one has gained more first downs (224); and only one other program gains more yards per snap (7.7).

The short answer is that coach Mario Cristobal has stockpiled talent; created a hotly competitive team environment; developed athletes into fierce football players; and, four years ago, took a giant leap: He hired Houston's offensive coordinator, then a somewhat unknown disciple of the Air Raid offense who, in his biggest job (Kentucky in 2015) lasted one season.

You can find that someone within that dimly lit room, his language sprinkled across wall and window, a man who's blended the pass-heavy concepts of Hal Mumme and Mike Leach with Cristobal's intensely physical running game to produce something altogether scary for opposing defenses.

"Adapt or die," Cristobal says from his office on hiring Dawson, perhaps not dissimilar to Nick Saban plucking Lane Kiffin in 2014 to reinvent his offense.

"Shannon has been able to morph the principles of the Air Raid with the power running game and screen game. He feels like we're just starting to hit our stride."

Now living near Jackson, Mississippi and, at least for now, out of coaching, Hal Mumme has watched the Hurricanes enough to recognize his system, as well as the country-talk'n Louisiana man who paces the sideline and who he hired in 2003.

Upon taking the job to revive the Southeastern Louisiana football program, Mumme met with a school donor and former player who'd shown up to his office solely to tell the coach that he should hire his son, a 20-something former Mississippi College quarterback.

Great! Mumme thought after the meeting. Another helicopter dad!

Mumme met with Ricky Dawson's son and, wishing not to hire a booster's boy, intentionally described to him the single-most awful job on his staff: a do-anything-for-almost-nothing gig that included chauffeuring Mumme to and from fundraising events when the coach drank.

"I painted the worst picture you could paint for this guy," recalls Mumme, "and he goes, 'When do I start?'"

Months later, late in a tight rivalry game, Shannon dipped his head into the huddle and suggested Mumme run a play called Fox, where the quarterback fakes a screen and goes deep. Mumme began to berate the low-level staff member for injecting himself — until he realized Shannon was right.

He called Fox and the Lions scored the game-winning touchdown.

"I've been a Shannon Dawson fan ever since," Mumme said with a laugh.

Perhaps that was Ricky Dawson's best sales job — helping land his son the gig in Hammond, Louisiana.

A businessman and motivational speaker for most of his life, Ricky, with wife Carlette, raised two boys on several acres of family land in the bayous and backwoods community of Bluff Creek, an unincorporated settlement some 35 miles northeast of Baton Rouge — a place with no red light and one that even Shannon acknowledges is "very Louisiana country."

Ricky Dawson was an ideas man. And he could sell an idea to just about anyone. But many of his business ventures failed miserably, and at times, the family found itself broke. He never quit selling, though, never stopped thinking or believing. And he never brought the failures home to his family.

He always preached to his sons the power of positive thinking. "Attitude is a choice," he'd tell them. He'd find a way to make anything work for his boys, "even if I've got to get a wooden bill and pick s**t with the chickens," he'd tell them.

Shannon Dawson lives life like that now.

The glass is always half full. There is always light at the end of the tunnel.

He coaches that way, too: positive, calm, confident. He calls it "keeping the game small" — a recognition that it is still only a game.

"You get older and you find out that nothing is perfect. When I took a deep dive with dad through the years, through high school and college, it gave me an unbelievable appreciation for him," Shannon says. "Looking back on it, I appreciate the fact … there are very few people who can compartmentalize the negativity and have this outpouring of positivity. In his mind, it was all about the journey."

Dawson's own journey is typical of most career-long assistant coaches: ups, downs, big breaks, unceremonial firings and, at some point, a dejected man doubting his dream.

A few years after Mumme gave him that low-level gig, he reunited with his college coach, Dana Holgorsen, at West Virginia. There, he met wife Chelsea, now the mother of his two girls, while coordinating Holgorsen's Air Raid scheme with a (running) twist.

Then, things began declining. A "bad fit" in Lexington led to his firing (he holds no hard feelings and still communicates with then-coach Mark Stoops) and that gave way to a three-year grind as coordinator at Southern Miss that had him rethinking his coaching career.

He called his dad and brother back home in south Louisiana.

"Everybody has that point in their life in our profession," Dawson says. "I listened to [New Mexico coach] Jason Eck talk about that in an interview recently. I started thinking about mine and that Southern Miss deal beat me down. I hated football. I hated everything about it. It wasn't fun. I could see myself changing as a husband and dad."

A tough job in Hattiesburg was made more difficult by family trauma. While coordinating Southern Miss, his mother fought what would eventually be a losing battle against cancer. Thankfully, he could commute the 90 minutes to Bluff Creek to spend time with her in her final years.

Ricky and Carlette were college sweethearts. The two met while attending Southeastern Louisiana — the same place where Mumme gave Dawson his (little) break. Toward the end of Carlette's illness, she pulled her two boys aside and told them that Ricky had been acting funny and that, after she passed, they needed to get a doctor's evaluation.

Ricky was diagnosed with Parkinson's not longer afterward.

There are few questions that Cooper Barkate can't answer.

The Miami receiver is as sharp of a player as you'll meet — educated at Duke and then Harvard before that.

How has Miami integrated three straight transfer quarterbacks -—Cam Ward, Carson Beck and Darian Mensah — so seamlessly?

"That's a good question," he says, pausing to dig up an answer. "I don't know. I was talking to Darian [Mensah] when he came in and the coaches talked to Darian about what he likes and doesn't. It's not like they confined him to the same box as Carson Beck."

Cristobal and Dennis Smith, executive director of the program and one of the coach's chief recruiters, brought in some of the nation's most talented passers. It was Dawson's job to use them appropriately.

But he didn't plug each of them into his system. He molded his system to them — perhaps his greatest strength.

"That's the most fun part," says Mensah. "He calls plays that his players want to run. He doesn't fit players into his system — his system is the players."

At Miami, Dawson has refined this system of his — a marriage of the Air Raid passing concepts with more traditional NFL-style formations and run game. While Mumme sees his famous receiver route patterns when watching the Hurricanes — Y-Cross, Y-Sail, Stick, Mesh, Fox and all of the famous Air Raid screens — he also sees a team that aligns tightly using multiple backs and tight ends.

The Air Raid is more of a philosophy, Mumme says, rather than a scheme. Sure, there are the route concepts that he and Leach introduced to the mainstream while at Kentucky in the late 1990s. But the three principles of the mission are most important: (1) throw it short to someone who knows how to score; (2) throw it deep if they take away the short pass; and (3) run it if they take away the first two.

The short, crossing screen plays have been Miami's most potent weapon.

Quips Mumme: "Yeah, they're awesome at it. Mostly because they are throwing to Malachi Toney."

Dawson's ability to get his most slippery and electric weapon the ball is perhaps his best gift. Toney averages more catches a game (9.1) than all but one player in the nation. This week against Notre Dame, the offensive coordinator will need to do it without him. Toney sustained an ankle injury in practice that will require surgery and keep him out 4-6 weeks , sources told Yahoo Sports.

Meanwhile, Mensah and Barkate, each on their third school, say they've never had more control of an offense to change plays or routes before the snap. Barkate often adjusts his route just before or even after the snap based on the defense's formation.

"It's an NFL pro-style offense," he says.

Part of Dawson's refining of the system included shortening play calls by making "smaller words mean more" — an act of simplifying the offense for new quarterbacks. He describes his role as working "parallel with quarterbacks" as opposed to dictating to them — a luxury, perhaps, afforded to him by Cristobal's acquisition of the last three veteran passers.

"A lot of people make offensive football hard. And the reason is they put too much in the quarterback's brain. I'm trying to take s*** out of your brain," Dawson says.

But for all the strategic Xs and Os, one thing remains even more important, and that's something Dawson got from his old man.

"Attitude is just as important as the scheme — 50% of it or maybe more," he says.

A man known for his bruising style and relentless competitiveness, Cristobal left Oregon to return to his home to resurrect one of college football's most storied brands. He's got a locker room mostly full of "alphas," he calls them.

They have attitude. They have swagger. And they hold one another accountable.

Barkate has never seen anything like a Miami practice. Anyone slouching is immediately lambasted by a fellow player. "I've never been in that culture where it corrects itself," he says.

That's why integrating a quarterback isn't the difficult part, says Cristobal. "To me, the challenge is more selecting the right fit," he says. "The rest naturally takes off. It's an environment where iron sharpens iron."

After arriving in Miami this spring, Mensah began intentionally showing up at the facility as early as possible and stayed as long as possible. "You want people to see you and say 'This dude is always working,'" he says.

He wanted to be the first one into the facility. He learned that meant arriving at 5 a.m. if he wanted to beat Toney.

"When you have alphas get together, alphas need to respect each other," Cristobal says. "You can't respect someone unless you get to know them and you can't know them unless you invest time. Those two, they are an awesome match."

Back in Dawson's office more than just play designs are scribbled on his walls and window.

An inscription appears above his desk: Capacity for boredom.

He stole that phrase from Mumme and Leach and consistently preaches it to his staff and players. In short, it means "don't get tired of doing the same s*** over and over again," he says.

Don't like running the same route? Too bad, it's working.

Don't like blocking the same way? Suck it up, it's for the better.

Now on a multi-million dollar contract and presiding over the nation's top-ranked offense, Dawson acknowledges that he often pinches himself.

How did a Louisiana country boy who nearly quit the profession just seven years ago end up here?

"I'm overly blessed for what I got," he says. "It gives me the mentality of 'Enjoy it and do the best you can do.'"

He attributes the rejuvenation of his career to Cristobal and Holgorsen, who upon taking the Houston job in 2019 hired Dawson as his tight ends coach in a move that convinced him to remain in coaching. Over four years, Holgorsen promoted him to quarterbacks coach, pass-game coordinator and, finally, offensive coordinator.

And then came what Shannon calls today a "life-changing deal to me": an interview with Cristobal for the coordinator position at a place rich with talent.

"That interview was a defining moment," he says. "I never went into a game with a sense of urgency as I did that interview. I knew who I was up against. I got interviewed late. I knew I had to kill that interview. I didn't know if I would get that opportunity again."

Cristobal took the risk. He fired Josh Gattis after his first season in Coral Gables and hired a little-known Air Raid disciple to help him rebuild the Hurricanes.

As the Notre Dame-Miami game arrives this week, the two programs have returned to the glory years that marked one of the sport's nastiest and most intense rivalries — the "Convicts vs. Catholics" era of the 1980s, 90s and early 2000s. Last year, the Hurricanes beat the Irish to open the season in a result that ultimately kept Notre Dame out of the College Football Playoff and ushered Miami into a postseason where it won three games and reached, like the Irish in 2024, the national championship game.

The U is, indeed, back — and at a critical time in an evolving landscape where the Hurricanes are positioning themselves for a promotion .

"When I was playing [at Miami], we'd go to the parks with these little kids and ask, 'Who wants to be a Hurricane?' And every kid would raise their hands," Cristobal says. "We get back here in 2022 and go to the park and ask, 'Who wants to be a Hurricane?' One or two kids raised their hands. I look over at our people and go, 'That's what has gone wrong. The community has been lost.'

"Now, we show up and it looks like a scene from the Beatles," he says laughing.

On Saturday night, in Notre Dame Stadium, two programs meet with playoff implications on the line in a rivalry steeped in history and drama. A Louisiana boy will pace the sideline and call plays with much of his family watching back home.

Shannon still speaks to his father almost every day. Ricky is not well enough to attend games, but he remains active on Facebook. Ricky's page is littered with weekly posts reminding friends and family about his son's next big outing.

"Shannon's game ABC 6:30 channel 2," he wrote on Tuesday.

Mumme will be watching too, perhaps a split screen with Miami-Notre Dame and Kentucky-Tennessee, he says. He wouldn't be surprised if Shannon runs Fox, or any of the other Air Raid pass concepts scribbled along the coach's walls and window.

After all, this is a big one. It's time to pull out all the tricks.

Better yet, just keep feeding the talent, says Mumme.

"They are loaded and it makes you jealous," he says. "They're fun to watch and the one thing Shannon Dawson understands is put the ball in your playmakers' hands."

articles.title: Pepe Brasín, contundente con Vinicius: "Este Real Madrid con Vinicius es peor"
articles.standfirst: El periodista analizó junto a Pablo Villa en La Tribu de Radio MARCA el momento del conjunto blanco
articles.summary: El periodista analizó junto a Pablo Villa en La Tribu de Radio MARCA el momento del conjunto blanco
articles.body: Pepe Brasín ha repasado la actualidad de la Champions League en La Tribu de Radio MARCA. En su conversación con Pablo Villa, el periodista ha analizado el rendimiento de los equipos españoles en la competición europea, el gran momento de Bayern de Múnich y Borussia Dortmund y la situación del Real Madrid, con especial atención al papel de Vinicius y Arda Güler. Preguntado por las conclusiones que dejó la última victoria del conjunto blanco, Brasín fue contundente con el brasileño: "Este Real Madrid con Vinicius es peor, pero creo que es más relevante el que faltaba". Una reflexión que le sirvió para poner en valor la figura del futbolista turco: "Creo que el mejor jugador de la temporada, quitando Courtois, es Arda Güler; y sin Arda Güler este equipo es peor". El periodista tampoco escondió su preocupación por el rendimiento del extremo madridista. "Sin duda está jugando muy mal al fútbol, no trato de cambiar ni la dinámica del discurso ni el relato, está jugando mal", aseguró. Sin embargo, insistió en que la presencia del centrocampista podría haber cambiado la imagen del equipo: "Si ayer está Güler, estoy seguro que hasta Vinicius nos hubiera parecido mejor". Brasín también quiso detenerse en las derrotas del Atlético de Madrid y el Betis frente al Bayern de Múnich y el Borussia Dortmund, respectivamente: "La superioridad frente al equipo español del segundo escalón y equipo español del tercer escalón, que así podemos considerar tanto al Atlético como al Betis, me pareció muy notable". Especialmente elogioso se mostró con el Borussia Dortmund: "Hay fútbol ahí, hay físico, hay idea". Una valoración que acompañó de una conclusión sobre los dos grandes representantes de la Bundesliga: "Creo que son dos equipos que este año, quitando Madrid y Barça, son dos equipos que están por encima del fútbol español". Por último, Brasín pidió cautela a la hora de valorar la situación de los equipos españoles tras las primeras cuatro jornadas de la fase liga. "En un calendario asimétrico de tal calibre como es la Champions League, sacar cualquier tipo de conclusión a cuatro jornadas me parece un poco absurdo", señaló.

articles.title: Loren mantiene la fe en Funes
articles.standfirst: El entrenador cuenta con la confianza del director deportivo
articles.summary: El entrenador cuenta con la confianza del director deportivo
articles.body: El Málaga no contempla actualmente la destitución de Juanfran Funes en caso de que el equipo caiga derrotado ante el Racing. La continuidad del técnico no está condicionada a un único resultado, salvo que se produzca un descalabro de grandes dimensiones o que la respuesta de La Rosaleda alcance un nivel de indignación que obligue a replantear el escenario. Loren Juarros sigue siendo el principal respaldo del entrenador y conserva capacidad de decisión en este asunto. El director deportivo mantiene su apuesta por el técnico de Loja, aunque la urgencia de sumar una victoria y la sucesión de jornadas sin conseguirla están erosionando progresivamente la confianza en el proyecto que ambos lideran. La postura de Loren recuerda, en cierta medida, a la que mantuvo con Sergio Pellicer. El burgalés fue partidario de sostener al anterior entrenador mientras consideró que todavía había margen para reconducir la situación, hasta que el deterioro resultó insostenible. Ese mismo planteamiento es el que pretende aplicar ahora con Funes, una apuesta personal desde su llegada a Martiricos y uno de los entrenadores en los que más ha confiado desde que asumió la dirección deportiva. Sin embargo, la aparente calma que se intenta trasladar desde el club no impide que el mercado empiece a moverse alrededor del banquillo blanquiazul. El Málaga ya está recibiendo contactos para conocer de primera mano cómo está la situación. Algunos llegan directamente a la dirección deportiva, mientras que otros utilizan intermediarios para hacer llegar sus propuestas a las altas instancias de la entidad. Por el momento, la respuesta del club pasa por remitirse a Loren Juarros. La posibilidad de dirigir al Málaga en Primera División supone un atractivo importante y son varios los técnicos sin equipo que ya valoran, de manera discreta, la opción de recalar en La Rosaleda. No es una situación excepcional. Cuando la continuidad de un entrenador empieza a generar dudas, el mercado suele adelantarse a cualquier decisión oficial. Ya ocurrió la pasada temporada, cuando varios técnicos fueron vistos en las gradas de La Rosaleda durante los momentos más delicados de Pellicer. Una de las imágenes más recordadas fue la de Bolo presenciando desde el estadio el encuentro en el que el entonces entrenador malaguista consiguió salvar su puesto con una contundente victoria por 3-0 ante el Deportivo. Funes, mientras tanto, mantiene el foco en encontrar soluciones deportivas y cambiar la dinámica del equipo. El técnico que devolvió al Málaga a Primera ocho años después es consciente, no obstante, de todo lo que se está generando a su alrededor. Las pintadas aparecidas en su contra no le han hecho cambiar su planteamiento, aunque sí las considera injustas, tal y como ha trasladado a su entorno más próximo. Su continuidad cuenta, a día de hoy, con el respaldo de Loren Juarros. La incógnita está en conocer hasta qué punto el propio director deportivo conserva el apoyo necesario dentro del club para sostener su decisión. En este sentido, conviene recordar las dificultades que rodearon la renovación del burgalés la pasada temporada, pese a los buenos resultados deportivos del equipo. Un antecedente que cobra especial relevancia en el momento actual y que invita a no limitar el análisis de la crisis únicamente al banquillo.

articles.title: Así es la nueva camiseta Y-3 del Real Madrid: regresa el icónico diseño del dragón
articles.standfirst: Adidas reedita junto al club blanco la tercera equipación de la temporada 2014-15, diseñada por Yohji Yamamoto, con el emblemático dragón de dos cabezas como protagonista.
articles.summary: Adidas reedita junto al club blanco la tercera equipación de la temporada 2014-15, diseñada por Yohji Yamamoto, con el emblemático dragón de dos cabezas como protagonista.
articles.body: El Real Madrid y adidas han presentado una reedición de la camiseta Y-3 Dragon, uno de los diseños más reconocibles de la historia reciente del club. La nueva prenda recupera la estética de la tercera equipación de la temporada 2014-15, fruto de la primera colaboración entre la entidad blanca y el diseñador japonés Yohji Yamamoto. La camiseta mantiene el característico dragón de dos cabezas que ocupa la parte frontal sobre un fondo gris carbón oscuro. Una ilustración que convirtió aquella equipación en una de las más singulares del fútbol y que vuelve ahora con una reproducción del diseño original. Yohji Yamamoto incorporó elementos inspirados en la simbología oriental. El dragón representa la fuerza, la ambición y el poder, mientras que el motivo del ave hace referencia a la agilidad y la habilidad. Una propuesta que en 2014-15 rompió con los diseños habituales de las equipaciones de fútbol al combinar deporte y moda. Aquella camiseta fue lucida por algunos de los principales jugadores del Real Madrid y adquirió con el paso del tiempo un importante valor entre coleccionistas y aficionados. Su regreso recupera una de las colaboraciones más reconocibles entre adidas y el club blanco. La colección Y-3 Bring Back incluye también una chaqueta y unos pantalones de chándal inspirados en la línea original de 2014-15. Las prendas ya están disponibles en las tiendas adidas, distribuidores seleccionados y en la tienda online de la marca. Nacido en Tokio en 1943, Yohji Yamamoto es uno de los nombres más reconocidos de la moda contemporánea. Junto a Rei Kawakubo, fundadora de Comme des Garçons, contribuyó a llevar la vanguardia japonesa a las pasarelas de París durante los años ochenta. El negro, las siluetas amplias y la ausencia de adornos son algunos de los rasgos característicos de su trabajo. Su relación con adidas comenzó en 2002, cuando ambas partes crearon Y-3, una línea que combina moda y ropa deportiva. La colaboración abrió una nueva vía de conexión entre la industria del deporte y los diseñadores de alta costura. La camiseta del Real Madrid de 2014 trasladó esa propuesta al fútbol, con un diseño que rompió con los códigos estéticos habituales de las equipaciones. La equipación salió a la venta a finales de agosto de 2014 y el Real Madrid la utilizó principalmente en la Champions League, durante la temporada posterior a la conquista de la Décima. En aquella plantilla destacaban Cristiano Ronaldo, Benzema y Bale, además de los recién llegados James Rodríguez y Toni Kroos. También formaba parte del equipo Javier 'Chicharito' Hernández, cuya presencia contribuyó a que la camiseta despertara un interés especial entre los aficionados mexicanos. No es la primera vez que el dragón vuelve a protagonizar una colección. En octubre de 2020, adidas y Pharrell Williams presentaron HUMANRACE, una línea que reinterpretó equipaciones históricas de clubes como Arsenal, Bayern de Múnich, Juventus, Manchester United y Real Madrid. Para el conjunto blanco, Pharrell eligió precisamente el diseño de 2014. En lugar de reproducirlo, modificó la ilustración del dragón mediante una técnica de pintura al agua aplicada a mano, que difuminaba sus contornos y generaba un efecto visual diferente. Aquella versión fue una edición de colección y no llegó a utilizarse en partidos oficiales. La colaboración entre el diseñador japonés y el club blanco tuvo otro capítulo en marzo de 2022, con motivo del 120 aniversario de la entidad. Yamamoto diseñó una cuarta equipación negra con líneas diagonales inspiradas en la estética de un jardín zen y el logotipo de Y-3 en lugar del de adidas. El Real Madrid estrenó aquella camiseta en un Clásico disputado en el Santiago Bernabéu. La reedición de 2026 recupera ahora uno de los diseños más reconocibles de esa relación. adidas considera la Y-3 Dragon una de las camisetas de fútbol más coleccionables del siglo XXI. Las unidades originales han adquirido un valor especial en el mercado de segunda mano, lo que convierte este nuevo lanzamiento en una oportunidad para quienes no pudieron conseguirla en 2014.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane extends contract with Bayern Munich deal until 2029
articles.summary: Harry Kane's remarkable journey at Bayern Munich has received another major chapter, with the England captain signing a contract extension that will keep
articles.body: Harry Kane's remarkable journey at Bayern Munich has received another major chapter, with the England captain signing a contract extension that will keep him at the German giants until June 2029. Fresh from becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or, the prolific striker has committed his future to the Bundesliga champions, bringing an end to speculation surrounding his long-term plans.Bayern Munich confirmed the agreement on Thursday, November 5, extending Kane's previous contract, which was due to expire in 2027, by another two years. The announcement comes after months of negotiations between the club and the 33-year-old, who had repeatedly expressed his happiness in Munich and his desire to continue playing for the German champions.Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2023 and has since established himself as one of the most influential players in European football. He has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances for the club.'I feel right at home': Kane opens up on Bayern stayExpressing his delight at extending his stay, Kane said his decision was influenced by his strong connection with the club, the supporters and the city of Munich. The England captain also highlighted the happiness of his family and his relationship with manager Vincent Kompany."I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager," Kane said."It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen also welcomed the development, describing Kane's extension as a significant moment for the club and its supporters.From Tottenham heartbreak to Bayern successKane's decision to leave Tottenham in 2023 was driven by his ambition to win major trophies, having spent nearly two decades associated with the north London club without securing a senior team honour.His move to Germany has proved transformative. Since arriving at the Allianz Arena, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB Cup and two Franz Beckenbauer Supercups. He has also finished as the Bundesliga's leading scorer in each of his first three seasons in Germany, becoming the first player to achieve that feat.The striker's individual numbers have been equally impressive. He has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances for Bayern, including 101 goals in his first 98 Bundesliga appearances, becoming the fastest player to reach the century mark in the competition.He has also won the European Golden Shoe twice, in the 2023-24 and 2025-26 seasons, underlining his consistency at the highest level.Ballon d'Or triumph caps remarkable seasonKane's contract extension follows the biggest individual achievement of his career. On October 26, he was crowned the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or winner, becoming the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to receive football's most prestigious individual honour. He also became the first Bundesliga-based player in 30 years to win the award.The England captain edged out competition from Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal after an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, during which he scored 73 goals for club and country across all competitions.His remarkable scoring record played a crucial role in Bayern's domestic success, while his performances for England further strengthened his credentials. Kane also finished as the Champions League's second-highest scorer with 14 goals as Bayern reached the semi-finals. He subsequently captained England to a third-place finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, scoring six goals in the tournament.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Douvikas, el goleador que el Celta sí tenía: cómo Cesc convirtió una promesa intermitente en un delantero de 14 goles
articles.standfirst: Continuidad y un sistema que potencia sus virtudes, claves en el rendimiento del griego
articles.summary: Continuidad y un sistema que potencia sus virtudes, claves en el rendimiento del griego
articles.body: Cuando Anastasios Douvikas abandonó el Celta de Vigo rumbo al Como de Cesc Fàbregas, la sensación general era que el delantero griego había dejado más dudas que certezas en Balaídos. Hoy es pichichi de la Champions. Sin embargo, una mirada a los números desmonta parte de ese relato: Douvikas no fracasó en Vigo. Lo que encontró en Italia fue algo que nunca tuvo de forma continuada en Galicia: confianza, titularidad y un ecosistema diseñado para potenciar sus virtudes. La prueba más contundente está en sus cifras. Durante la temporada 2023-24 marcó siete goles en apenas 905 minutos de Liga con el Celta. Traducido a rendimiento puro, suponía un tanto cada 129 minutos, una frecuencia propia de delanteros de primer nivel. Su promedio de 0,70 goles por 90 minutos fue incluso superior al que ha registrado posteriormente en una temporada completa en Italia. El problema era que aquellos números convivían con una realidad muy diferente: Douvikas rara vez logró sentirse indiscutible. Llegó procedente del FC Utrecht tras una campaña espectacular en la que firmó 19 goles en la Eredivisie, compartiendo además el título de máximo goleador de la competición. Sin embargo, en Vigo alternó titularidades y suplencias, acumulando apenas 1.605 minutos ligueros entre temporada y media. Nueve meses con Rafa Benítez, y otros nueve con Claudio Giráldez. La comparación con su etapa en el Como resulta reveladora. En la temporada 2025-26 disputó 2.273 minutos en la Serie A y alcanzó los 14 goles. Su media bajó ligeramente hasta un gol cada 162 minutos, pero la diferencia es que mantuvo ese rendimiento durante toda una campaña ejerciendo como referencia ofensiva del equipo. Ahí aparece la mano de Cesc. El técnico español no ha transformado al futbolista. Más bien ha construido un contexto que le permite explotar aquello que siempre tuvo. Douvikas nunca ha destacado por su participación en la elaboración, ni por bajar constantemente a asociarse, ni por convertirse en un delantero generador de juego. Su mayor virtud sigue siendo la misma que exhibía en Países Bajos y en Vigo: ocupar bien el área, atacar espacios cortos, ganar duelos en el remate y necesitar muy pocas ocasiones para marcar. En el Como recibe más balones en zonas de finalización y disfruta de una continuidad competitiva que le permite encadenar semanas y meses sin la incertidumbre del banquillo. Los 14 goles de la pasada temporada no representan tanto una reinvención del jugador como la consolidación de un perfil que ya asomaba en Balaídos.

articles.title: Women's Super League: ACL injuries in women's football
articles.summary: The Football Association and WSL Football launch a major research project to better understand why ACL injuries occur in women's football.
articles.body:
The Football Association and WSL Football have launched a major research project to better understand why anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries occur in women's football and identify ways to reduce them.

Funded by the FA, the PhD study with Imperial College London and sports knee surgeon Simon Ball will be led by researcher Hanna Lehtovirta and involve clubs across the Women's Super League and WSL2.

ACL injuries are among the most serious issues facing the women's game, often keeping players out for months.

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer the injury than their male counterparts.

Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead, Leah Williamson and Sam Kerr are among the players to have suffered the injury over recent years.

While previous studies have highlighted potential risk factors including anatomical, hormonal, biomechanical and environmental influences, researchers say less is known about how those factors interact in the day-to-day experience of elite football.

The study aims to provide one of the most comprehensive examinations of ACL injuries in women's football by combining scientific data with the experiences of players and staff.

Players from every WSL and WSL2 club will be invited to take part, alongside medical, performance and coaching staff.

The research will be conducted in two phases.

The first will use player surveys to gather data on injury history, training and match load, and hormonal, nutritional and psychological factors.

Data from players who have suffered ACL injuries since 2018-19 will be compared with those who have not.

The second phase will involve interviews with players and staff to explore perceptions of ACL injuries and current approaches to training and prevention.

Researchers hope the findings will help shape future injury prevention, rehabilitation and player welfare strategies in the women's game.

In April 2025, Fifa announced they were also funding research into whether hormonal fluctuations during menstrual cycles could be contributing to the rise in ACL injuries in women's football.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires: Portugal forward quits international football
articles.summary: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".
articles.body:
Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says he is retiring from international football.

The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003.

He walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine and a 30-day suspension.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. , external

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

"Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart.

"A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end."

On Friday Portugal will announce their squad for this month's Nations League fixtures - against Denmark at home and Wales away.

The PFF said it will not "let this farewell take place without due tribute".

A statement read: "It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo's immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much."

Ronaldo played in six European Championships. Portugal were runners-up in 2004 and champions in 2016, but did not progress beyond the semi-finals of the World Cup during his career.

Portugal captain since 2008, he won the inaugural Nations League in 2019 and in 2025.

Ronaldo's great rival and Argentina legend Lionel Messi retired from international football on an emotional night in front of an 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires in October.

Why did Ronaldo fall out with Portugal coach?

Ronaldo started every match in his sixth World Cup this summer, when Portugal lost to eventual champions Spain in the last 16.

His peformances in the tournament drew criticism in the media, with many observers questioning if he remained a force at international level.

He fell out with new coach Jorge Jesus after being named as a substitute against Norway.

Ronaldo was reportedly angry at being made to warm up in the second half but not brought on - the first time he was an unused substitute in a competitive Portugal game since 2008.

When Jesus said Ronaldo would not start against Denmark, Ronaldo left the camp and issued a lengthy statement in which he said he would not be retiring and that Jesus had twice "broke his word".

Jesus said the door remained open for a return, while the PFF fined Ronaldo and suspended him for 30 days - a period that did not include any Portugal games.

Ronaldo did not reference the falling-out in his farewell video, but acknowledged that he had made mistakes.

"There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes; I suffered," he said.

"There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today I realise my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world."

articles.title: Karl Robinson: Bromley appoint former MK Dons and Oxford United boss
articles.summary: League One's bottom side Bromley name former MK Dons and Oxford United boss Karl Robinson as their new manager.
articles.body:
League One's bottom side Bromley have named former MK Dons and Oxford United boss Karl Robinson as their new manager.

Robinson, 46, who has been out of work since leaving Salford City in June , has signed a "long-term contract".

Byron Webster, who took interim charge following the sacking of Andy Woodman last month, will stay at Bromley as part of Robinson's coaching staff.

The Ravens are three points from the safety line in League One after winning promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last season.

"Karl brings an elite level of experience, tactical acumen, and a proven track record of competing at the sharp end of League One," chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves told the club website.

"His relentless energy matches our ambition perfectly, and we are unified in our vision to drive this football club forward into an exciting new era.

"I led a full recruitment process, which began the day after our previous manager's departure. From the outset, my intention was to find someone who had worked at this level and had the experience and qualities to take Bromley Football Club on the next stage of its journey.

"It was important to take the time to work through that process thoroughly, and I am delighted that it has brought us to Karl."

Robinson's first game in charge will be Saturday's FA Cup first-round meeting with Rotherham United, who are managed by his former number two at Salford, Alex Bruce.

Woodman, who was dismissed on 22 October, guided the club to two promotions in three seasons but left after two wins in the first 10 games this term.

Robinson spent more than six years in charge of MK Dons, which included a 4-0 League Cup win over Manchester United in October 2014, and promotion to the Championship seven months later after finishing runners-up in League One.

The team suffered immediate relegation and he was sacked by the Dons in October 2016.

Robinson then spent 16 months in charge of Charlton Athletic, departing by mutual consent in March 2018 and immediately being named the new Oxford United boss.

He twice took the U's to the League One play-offs, before losing his job in February 2023.

After a spell as assistant manager at Leeds United, Robinson took over at Salford City in January 2024, and last season led the club to their highest ever finish, of fourth in League Two.

However, they lost the play-off final to Notts County and Robinson was surprisingly sacked.

articles.title: La familia de Jesús de Miguel: "Necesitamos vivir este duelo en la tranquilidad que esta situación requiere"
articles.standfirst: Los familiares del futbolista han agradecido las innumerables muestras de cariño recibidas en los últimos días y han solicitado que se respete su privacidad mientras afrontan la pérdida
articles.summary: Los familiares del futbolista han agradecido las innumerables muestras de cariño recibidas en los últimos días y han solicitado que se respete su privacidad mientras afrontan la pérdida
articles.body: La familia de Jesús ha querido pronunciarse públicamente para agradecer el apoyo recibido tras el fallecimiento del futbolista. A través de un emotivo comunicado emitido por Manuel Hernández, representante del jugador, los familiares han dado las gracias por los mensajes, llamadas y gestos de afecto llegados desde todos los ámbitos del fútbol y de la sociedad. "No tenemos palabras suficientes para agradecer cada mensaje, cada llamada y cada gesto de afecto que nos está llegando", señala la familia, que ha querido extender su reconocimiento a compañeros, amigos, aficionados y clubes que han mostrado sus condolencias durante estos días. El comunicado destaca también la huella personal que dejó Jesús en quienes compartieron camino con él. "Sentir tanto cariño hacia Jesús y comprobar la huella que ha dejado en tantas personas es algo que siempre llevaremos con nosotros", afirma la familia. Junto al agradecimiento, los allegados del futbolista han lanzado una petición clara. "Pedimos desde el máximo respeto que se preserve nuestra intimidad y la de todas las personas que nos están acompañando en estos momentos. Necesitamos vivir este duelo en la tranquilidad que esta situación requiere", explican. La nota concluye con un recuerdo cargado de emoción hacia Jesús: "Jesús deja un vacío imposible de llenar, pero también un recuerdo inmenso en todos los que hemos tenido la suerte de compartir nuestra vida con él. Gracias por quererle, por recordarle y por acompañarnos". Un mensaje sereno y agradecido con el que la familia ha querido corresponder al enorme cariño recibido mientras afronta uno de los momentos más difíciles de sus vidas. En estos momentos tan difíciles para nosotros, queremos agradecer de corazón todas las palabras, todas las muestras de cariño que estamos recibiendo tras el fallecimiento de Jesús. No tenemos palabras suficientes para agradecer cada mensaje, cada llamada y cada gesto de afecto que nos está llegando. Gracias a todas las personas que se han acordado de él, a sus compañeros, amigos, aficionados y a todos los clubes que han querido trasladarnos sus condolencias y acompañarnos en este momento tan doloroso. Sentir tanto cariño hacia Jesús y comprobar la huella que ha dejado en tantas personas es algo que siempre llevaremos con nosotros. Por ello, pedimos desde el máximo respeto que se preserve nuestra intimidad y la de todas las personas que nos están acompañando en estos momentos. Necesitamos vivir este duelo en la tranquilidad que esta situación así requiere. Entendemos el cariño, el interés y las muestras de apoyo que está despertando su pérdida y os estamos profundamente agradecidos. Jesús deja un vacío imposible de llenar, pero también un recuerdo inmenso en todos los que hemos tenido la suerte de compartir nuestra vida con él. Gracias por quererle, por recordarle y por acompañarnos. Su familia.

articles.summary: Rueda de Prensa del inglés tras estampar su firma con el club bávaro hasta 2029
articles.body: harry Kane ha hablado en Múnich en la rueda de Prensa de anuncio oficial de su renovación con el Bayern hasta 2029, cosa que se ha hecho pública este jueves. Acompañado de la plana mayor del Bayern, Harry expresó sus primeros pensamientos tras este hito. La renovación. "No tuve que pensármelo mucho. Estoy en el mejor sitio que puedo imaginar. Firmamos el contrato ayer, pero la decisión se tomó hace mucho tiempo. No quisimos hablar por el Mundial, luego volvimos de allí y solo quedaban por ultimar los detalles. Como ya he dicho, sé que estoy en un equipo fantástico, que luchamos por la Liga de Campeones y por todos los títulos. Para mí es importante estar en un lugar donde pueda mejorar y luchar por todo". El Bayern. "Fue fácil para mí. Si no creyera en el equipo, si no creyera en los títulos más importantes, habría buscado otras opciones. Me siento mejor que nunca. En los próximos años jugaremos, sin duda, al más alto nivel. Estoy muy feliz aquí, sé hacia dónde se dirige el equipo y creo en el proyecto; nunca he tenido dudas. Sin duda, la Champions es un gran objetivo para todos. Mientras sienta que estamos luchando por ello, me entusiasma la oportunidad de conseguirlo. Últimamente se ha hablado mucho de mí, pero estoy deseando volver a hablar menos y jugar más. Es importante que, como club, hayamos disfrutado de este momento; han sido momentos importantes en nuestra historia. Pero lo más importante es el partido, el juego, e intento expresarme en el campo; ahora se calmará todo y volveremos a la normalidad. Queremos dominar en Alemania, pero también ganar la Liga de Campeones. Estaré aquí hasta 2029 y mentiría si dijera que no quiero ganar al menos una Liga de Campeones para entonces. Es una presión, pero la afronto con ilusión". Los motivos. "Pasé mucho tiempo en la Premier League, siempre la he seguido de cerca. Está bien cambiar de aires. Múnich es un lugar maravilloso. A mi familia y a mí nos gusta ir al bosque y a la montaña. A mi hija mayor le gusta montar a caballo. Aquí hay todo eso. Y, a veces, un cambio así también sienta muy bien a nivel mental. Hemos conocido a nuevos amigos y una nueva cultura. Cuando sea mayor, echaré la vista atrás y diré: 'Fue un paso acertado y positivo salir de mi zona de confort'". El alemán. "Sabía que me iban a preguntar esto. Espero aprender un poco más en los próximos tres años que en los anteriores. He hablado con mi profesor de alemán, entiendo más que antes, pero sigo aprendiendo. Ahora tengo que hablar más y preocuparme menos por los errores y las reacciones que estos puedan provocar. Estoy aprendiendo poco a poco, pero espero poder conceder pronto una entrevista en alemán. Sé que a todos les haría mucha ilusión". Por su parte, Jan-Christian Dreesen, director general del club, habló sobre el que dicen va a ser el mejor contrato de un jugador en Europa en los próximos tres años. "Hace tres años, ese fue nuestro fichaje más importante. Pero Harry valió cada céntimo, en muchos sentidos. Es el motor del equipo, hace que sus compañeros jueguen mejor y es un ejemplo a seguir fuera del deporte. Si queremos seguir siendo atractivos y competir al más alto nivel europeo, tenemos que ser fuertes económicamente. Queremos aprovechar al máximo cada céntimo que ganamos para ser lo mejor posible. Y si el mejor jugador del mundo recibe un contrato de primera, es lógico. Queremos ser sólidos y actuar con sensatez económica. Pero también queremos tener el mejor equipo y ganar. No es fácil frente al poderío económico de otros clubes, pero lo estamos consiguiendo bastante bien".

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty: 10 record-breaking numbers from his legendary 23-year international career
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially retired from international football after an illustrious 23-year career with Portugal. Explore 10 record-breaking achievements he leaves behind, including being the all-time top scorer in men's international football with 146 goals.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo's international career has come to an end after 23 years, six World Cups and three major trophies with Portugal. The 41-year-old leaves the national team as the most-capped player and highest scorer in men's international football history, with 234 appearances and 146 goals. His departure closes a chapter that transformed Portugal's record books and established him among the most decorated players in the history of the international game.Cristiano Ronaldo announces Portugal retirement in emotional videoRonaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, November 5, through a five-minute video shared on his official social media accounts, including X. The caption read “Portugal estará sempre em mim”, translated as “Portugal will always be in me”, a message he repeated at the end of the video.Reading from printed pages, Ronaldo addressed the Portuguese public directly, describing the decision as difficult and bringing to a close a journey that began in August 2003.“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our National Team.”He acknowledged the significance of the decision before confirming that his time representing Portugal on the pitch was over.“Today, my journey on the pitch with the National Team comes to an end. I leave with my head held high.”He finished by reflecting on what wearing Portugal's number 7 shirt had meant to him, making clear that his connection with the country would remain long after his playing career for the national team.“The number 7 shirt will remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me.”Ronaldo made his senior international debut in August 2003 and went on to represent Portugal across six World Cups and multiple European Championships. He captained the country to three major senior honours: the European Championship in 2016 and the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.Portugal's exit from the 2026 World Cup marked the end of his tournament career. The team lost 1-0 to Spain in the round of 16 in Dallas on July 6, with Ronaldo confirming afterwards that it had been his final World Cup appearance. He subsequently brought his international career to a close with a record 146 goals in 234 appearances.Cristiano Ronaldo's records in men's international footballRonaldo leaves Portugal with a collection of records that extends across international goalscoring, appearances, tournament football and longevity. Several of those achievements are global firsts, while others place him at the top of the European and Portuguese record books.1. Most international goals in men's football – 146Ronaldo finishes as the highest goalscorer in the history of men's international football, with 146 goals for Portugal. He broke the previous world record on September 1, 2021, when he scored twice against the Republic of Ireland in a World Cup qualifying match in Faro-Loulé.The goals took his international tally to 110 and 111, moving him beyond the previous benchmark of 109 set by former Iran striker Ali Daei. Daei had been the first male footballer to reach 100 international goals, establishing a landmark that Ronaldo eventually surpassed. Lionel Messi joined the group of players to have scored at least 100 international goals on March 28, 2023.Ronaldo's final tally of 146 extended the record considerably beyond the mark he inherited from Daei and made him the first player to reach that figure in men's international football.2. Most international appearances in men's football – 234Ronaldo also retires as the most-capped male international footballer, having represented Portugal 234 times. His appearances span more than two decades, from his debut in August 2003 through the 2026 international campaign.The record reflects his longevity at the highest level of international football, with Ronaldo remaining a regular presence for Portugal across successive generations of players, different managers and major tournament campaigns.He also became the first footballer to reach 200 senior international appearances, achieving the milestone against Iceland in June 2023. He went on to add another 34 caps before bringing his Portugal career to an end.3. First player to score at six different FIFA World CupsRonaldo became the first player in men's football history to score at six different editions of the FIFA World Cup. His goals came at the 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 and 2026 tournaments.The landmark was completed during Portugal's group-stage campaign at the 2026 World Cup, when he scored against Uzbekistan. Having already found the net at each of the five preceding tournaments, the goal made him the first player to score across six separate editions.His six appearances at the tournament also put him in a category of his own in terms of longevity, with his World Cup career stretching across 20 years.4. Second-most appearances in FIFA World Cup history – 27Ronaldo made 27 appearances across his six World Cup campaigns, leaving him second on the all-time list of appearances at the tournament. He also holds the record for the most World Cup appearances by a Portugal player.His tournament history began in Germany in 2006 and continued through South Africa in 2010, Brazil in 2014, Russia in 2018, Qatar in 2022 and the 2026 tournament in North America.5. Portugal's leading World Cup goalscorer – 11 goalsRonaldo scored 11 goals across his six World Cup appearances, making him Portugal's all-time leading scorer at the tournament.His goals came across different stages of his international career, from his first World Cup campaign in 2006 through to his final appearance in 2026. The tally also places him among the most prolific goalscorers in the competition's history.6. Most goals in UEFA European Championship final tournaments – 14Ronaldo holds the record for the most goals scored in the final tournaments of the UEFA European Championship, with 14. His goals came across six editions of the competition, another record for the most appearances at the tournament.He first featured at Euro 2004, when Portugal reached the final on home soil, and continued to represent his country at the tournaments in 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024. His record-breaking run across six editions made him one of the defining players in the competition's modern history.7. Most appearances at the European Championship final tournaments – 30Across those six tournaments, Ronaldo made 30 appearances, the highest total in the history of the European Championship. His record reflects his sustained involvement in the competition over two decades, from his first appearance as a young forward in 2004 to his later campaigns as Portugal captain.8. Most European Championship goals including qualifying – 55Ronaldo's European Championship goalscoring record extends beyond the final tournaments. Including qualifying matches, he scored 55 goals, giving him the highest overall tally in the competition's history.The figure combines his 14 goals at the final tournaments with his contributions during qualifying campaigns, where he repeatedly helped Portugal secure places at the competition. It is a measure of his influence across the entire European Championship cycle rather than only the matches played at the finals.9. Most hat-tricks in men's international football – 10Ronaldo also holds the record for the most hat-tricks in men's international football, with 10. The achievement underlines his goalscoring consistency for Portugal, with multiple goals in a match becoming a recurring feature of his international career.Alongside those 10 hat-tricks, he also scored four goals in a single international match on two occasions, further demonstrating the scale of his contribution to Portugal's attack.10. Goals in 23 consecutive calendar years for Portugal – 2004 to 2026Ronaldo scored for Portugal in 23 consecutive calendar years, from 2004 through to 2026. His international career began in August 2003, but his run of scoring in successive calendar years started the following year and continued without interruption until his final season.The record captures a level of sustained goalscoring across an unusually long international career, spanning his development from a young forward into Portugal's captain and all-time leading scorer.Three major international titles with PortugalRonaldo's individual records were accompanied by three major trophies with Portugal, the first senior international titles of his country's history in the competitions concerned.UEFA European Championship – 2016: Ronaldo captained Portugal to their first European Championship title in France. Portugal defeated the hosts 1-0 after extra time in the final, despite Ronaldo having to leave the match through injury in the first half. He remained involved from the touchline as his team secured the trophy.UEFA Nations League – 2019: Portugal won the inaugural Nations League tournament on home soil, defeating the Netherlands 1-0 in the final in Porto. Ronaldo captained the side and played a central role in their run to the title.UEFA Nations League – 2025: Portugal claimed their second Nations League title in 2025, giving Ronaldo a third major senior international trophy as captain. Following Portugal's exit from the 2026 World Cup, he referred to the three titles he had won with his country.Ronaldo's international career therefore ends with more than two decades of service, three major trophies, six World Cups and records for both goals and appearances that place him at the summit of men's international football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal national team
articles.summary: Ronaldo's retirement comes as he's been in the middle of a dispute with new national team coach Jorge Jesus.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo's international soccer career is over.

The 41-year-old star striker announced Thursday that he would be ending his time with the Portuguese men's national team. Ronaldo's retirement comes after a 30-day suspension following his dispute with new national team coach Jorge Jesus.

"The day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said in a five-minute retirement video.

Ronaldo's international career ends with 146 goals in 234 games across his 23-year career. He joined Lionel Messi as the only men to appear in six World Cups when they took the field during the 2026 tournament in the United States.

Ronaldo's last appearance came on Sept. 24 when he appeared in a Nations League game.

His club playing career continues in the Saudi Pro Leauge with Al Nassr. He made a big-dollar move to Saudi Arabia during the 2022-23 season after a high-profile falling out with Manchester United in his second stint with the club. Ronaldo, who had played at Real Madrid and Juventus between his times at United, returned to the club in 2021.

Jesus was appointed to be Portugal's manager following the team's ouster in the 2026 World Cup. A former coach of Ronaldo's at Al Nassr, Jesus started to look to a Portugal national team future that did not include Ronaldo in a significant role.

After Ronaldo was on the bench for a Sept. 27 Nations League game against Norway, he claimed on social media that Jesus broke multiple promises. He wrote a five-page letter with numerous claims about Jesus. In it, he even said he had talking points he wanted Jesus to share at a news conference about Ronaldo's importance to the national team.

The public conflict led to the 30-day suspension and Jesus said that the door was still open for a Ronaldo return to the national team.

The friction with Jesus highlighted the issue that Portugal has been dealing with for many seasons. Ronaldo, the team's captain, had become a liability on the pitch at times. No longer the physical force he once was, there were times where Portugal's attacking play would look smoother and more coherent without him on the field.

Ronaldo scored twice in a 5-0 win over an overpowered Uzbekistan in the group stage and had a penalty against Croatia during the World Cup. But Portugals' Round of 32 comeback against the Croatians really kicked into gear when Ronaldo was removed for Ruben Neves in the 81st minute. Thirteen minutes later, Gonçalo Ramos, the man who had moved into Ronaldo's striker position, scored the game-winning goal for Portugal to advance.

Portugal had been favored to win Group K, but draws against Colombia and DR Congo in its opener meant that Messi and Ronaldo wouldn't meet on the pitch for the final time.

Had both Argentina and Portugal finished first in their groups, they would have been on a collision course to meet in the quarterfinals. Instead, since Portugal finished second, they were on opposite sides of the bracket and Portugal lost to eventual World Cup champion Spain in the Round of 16.

Ronaldo retires as the career goals leader

After Messi's retirement from international soccer earlier this year, the two global superstars end their careers at the top of the all-time international goals list.

Ronaldo's 146 goals are 20 more than Messi and they came in 26 more appearances. Ronaldo ends his Portugal career with a goal rate of 0.62 per game. Messi's rate is 0.61.

It's another close data point in a decades-long comparison between the players, though Messi's late-career surge shifted the debate in his favor. Argentina won the 2022 World Cup and made the final this summer.

Though Portugal never came close to winning the World Cup during Ronaldo's tenure, it won the Euros in 2016 and has added Nations League titles in 2016 and 2025.

The Euro 2016 title came two years after Portugal crashed out of the World Cup in the group stage. Grouped with Ghana, the United States and Germany in the Group of Death, Portugal lost to Germany, tied the U.S. and beat Ghana. However, the USMNT advanced to the Round of 16 on goal differential ahead of Portugal.

Portugal hosted the Euros as it won its first major international tournament. Ronaldo was forced to leave the final against France after a hard tackle, but Eder's goal in extra time was enough for a 1-0 win. Ronaldo was given the Silver Boot with three goals and three assists during the tournament.

articles.title: Calero se planta ante las dudas: “No necesito apoyos ni refuerzos, estoy fuerte”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Oviedo asegura que no ha percibido ningún gesto extraño en el club, admite que Pachuca puede tomar decisiones rápidas y se aferra a su trayectoria para afrontar la visita a Cádiz
articles.summary: El técnico del Oviedo asegura que no ha percibido ningún gesto extraño en el club, admite que Pachuca puede tomar decisiones rápidas y se aferra a su trayectoria para afrontar la visita a Cádiz
articles.body: Julián Calero no esquivó las preguntas sobre su continuidad. Con el Oviedo obligado a reaccionar después de dos derrotas, el entrenador respondió con una reivindicación de su fortaleza personal y de la confianza que mantiene en su trabajo. “No necesito ni apoyos, ni refuerzos, ni nada por el estilo, porque estoy fuerte”, proclamó en la previa de la visita al Cádiz. Su mensaje fue tan claro como su conocimiento de las reglas del oficio: “El Grupo Pachuca siempre ha tomado decisiones cuando han considerado y además muchas veces muy pronto”. El técnico rechazó presentarse como alguien a la espera de una ratificación desde los despachos. “Eso lo necesita quien se siente débil, yo no me siento débil”, insistió. Y dio la vuelta a la pregunta sobre el respaldo de la propiedad: a su juicio, debe ser él quien transmita al club “esa tranquilidad, esa seguridad y esa capacidad” para alcanzar los objetivos. Tampoco aseguró tener garantías sobre su futuro. “Esas cosas yo no las puedo saber, eso habría que preguntárselo a ellos”, señaló cuando se le planteó si conserva la misma consideración que al inicio. Calero dijo que no ha detectado señales de distanciamiento. “En el club no he notado ninguna situación rara ni cara rara”, explicó, antes de aceptar que el resultado terminará marcando el rumbo: “Esto es fútbol y lo que tenga que pasar va a pasar”. Mientras tanto, reivindicó sus 25 años en los banquillos y su decisión de no abandonar: “No me rindo jamás, pase lo que pase”. Su discurso de firmeza no ocultó la autocrítica. El entrenador admitió que, tras doce jornadas, el equipo todavía no ha encontrado la consistencia que busca, ni con balón ni sin él. También lamentó la facilidad con la que se ha visto dos goles por debajo en partidos recientes. Le satisface la reacción posterior, pero quiere evitar que cada intento de remontada nazca de una desventaja tan grande. “El fútbol te da segundas oportunidades si tú eres capaz de sostenerte en los partidos”, razonó. Las lesiones han condicionado, según su análisis, la construcción del equipo y sus constantes cambios de dibujo. Ahora dispone de más alternativas en las bandas, aunque advierte de que recuperar efectivos no significa recuperar inmediatamente su mejor nivel. Carlos Fernández, que ya trabaja de forma progresiva con el grupo, podría volver a estar disponible durante este mes. En Cádiz, Calero espera un adversario más sólido desde el relevo en el banquillo, con orden y peligro al contragolpe. Su prioridad, sin embargo, está dentro: que el Oviedo vuelva a parecerse al equipo que pretende construir y consiga los tres puntos. El entrenador asegura sentirse “tranquilo, feliz, seguro y trabajando”. El sábado será el campo el que mida la eficacia de esa convicción.

articles.title: El Eintracht de Frankfurt se interesa por Buba Sangaré
articles.standfirst: El conjunto alemán ya ha mantenido los primeros contactos con el entorno del lateral del Elche, una de las grandes promesas y activos económicos de la entidad franjiverde
articles.summary: El conjunto alemán ya ha mantenido los primeros contactos con el entorno del lateral del Elche, una de las grandes promesas y activos económicos de la entidad franjiverde
articles.body: El Eintracht de Frankfurt ha comenzado a mover ficha para hacerse con los servicios de Buba Sangaré. El conjunto alemán ha mantenido los primeros contactos con el entorno del futbolista ilicitano, tal y como ha adelantado Matteo Moretto. El lateral derecho del Elche se ha convertido en una de las grandes joyas de la plantilla y en uno de los activos con mayor proyección económica del club franjiverde. Sangaré llegó al Martínez Valero en calidad de cedido durante el pasado mercado invernal. Su incorporación respondió a la necesidad de cubrir la salida de Álvaro Núñez y reforzar el carril derecho. A las órdenes de Eder Sarabia disputó 12 encuentros y fue creciendo con el paso de las jornadas hasta consolidarse como una alternativa de garantías en el equipo. Su rendimiento convenció a la dirección deportiva del Elche, que el pasado mes de junio decidió ejecutar la opción de compra acordada con la Roma por 4,5 millones de euros. Una apuesta por un futbolista joven, con margen de crecimiento y un importante potencial de revalorización, un movimiento que caracteriza a Bragarnik. Su progresión no se detuvo ahí. Apenas un mes después, Buba Sangaré se proclamó campeón de Europa sub-19, un éxito que reforzó su proyección internacional. Esta temporada, bajo las órdenes de Anselmi, el defensa también está teniendo protagonismo en el carril derecho. Ya acumula diez partidos disputados e incluso ha estrenado su cuenta goleadora. El interés del Eintracht de Frankfurt vuelve a poner el foco en la capacidad del Elche para generar valor a través de jóvenes talentos. La entidad franjiverde ha demostrado en los últimos mercados que cuenta con futbolistas capaces de despertar el interés de clubes importantes y protagonizar operaciones de gran calado económico. Los precedentes más recientes son los traspasos de Rodrigo Mendoza, por 16 millones de euros, y Álvaro Rodríguez, por 25 millones después de apenas una temporada en el Martínez Valero. Ahora, Buba Sangaré aparece en el radar de otro club europeo. Su juventud, su proyección y el rendimiento que está ofreciendo convierten al lateral en una pieza de gran valor para el presente y el futuro del Elche. Por el momento, el interés del Eintracht se encuentra en una fase inicial de contactos, aunque su nombre ya empieza a ganar protagonismo en el mercado.

articles.body: El Getafe se quiere quitar el mal sabor de boca de la goleada del Lugano en el Coliseum de la pasada jornada de la Conference League con un triunfo que le permita, además, ascender en la clasificación. articles.title: From CR7's infamous World Cup wink to the Jorge Jesus row: 7 controversies that rocked Cristiano Ronaldo's career
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's glittering 23-year international career with Portugal has been defined by extraordinary goalscoring feats, major trophies and a
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo's glittering 23-year international career with Portugal has been defined by extraordinary goalscoring feats, major trophies and a collection of individual records. But alongside the success, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has also found himself at the centre of several controversies, both on and off the pitch.As the 41-year-old announced his decision to retire from international football after the November 2026 break, his final months in a Portugal shirt were also marked by a public fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. That episode added another chapter to a career in which Ronaldo's actions, comments and conduct have repeatedly made headlines.Here are seven major controversies that rocked the Portuguese superstar's career:Portugal camp walkout and fallout with Jorge JesusOne of the most recent controversies came during Portugal's September 2026 international camp. Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the team's 2-1 Nations League win over Norway on September 27, despite warming up during the match.Reports subsequently emerged that the forward had left the camp after a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus over his playing time. Ronaldo was said to be unhappy because he believed an agreement had been reached regarding his involvement.The episode prompted an investigation by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF). Ronaldo later apologised and said he would accept any punishment the governing body considered appropriate. On October 19, the Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary body handed him a 30-day suspension and a fine of 255 euros for leaving the national team camp without permission.The controversy came just weeks before Ronaldo announced his international retirement. While the timing invited questions about whether the fallout had influenced his decision, there was no confirmation that the dispute was the reason behind his announcement.ALSO READ: Cristiano Ronaldo bids emotional farewell to national team; Read full speechExplosive Piers Morgan interview and Manchester United exitRonaldo's second spell at Manchester United ended acrimoniously in November 2022 after an explosive interview with British broadcaster Piers Morgan.In the interview, released in two parts, Ronaldo criticised the club's hierarchy, questioned its infrastructure and said he felt "betrayed". He also said he had no respect for manager Erik ten Hag, claiming the Dutchman had not shown him respect.The comments sparked a major fallout with United. On November 22, 2022, the club announced that Ronaldo had left by mutual agreement, bringing his second stint at Old Trafford to an abrupt end.Phone incident involving an Everton supporterIn April 2022, Ronaldo was involved in an incident after Manchester United's 1-0 defeat to Everton at Goodison Park.As he walked towards the tunnel, the forward slapped a phone out of the hand of a spectator, later identified as a young Everton supporter. Footage of the incident circulated widely on social media.Ronaldo admitted that his conduct was improper, but did not admit the allegation of violent conduct. An independent FA commission subsequently found that his actions were both improper and violent, handing him a two-match suspension and a 50,000-pound fine.Spanish tax fraud caseRonaldo's time at Real Madrid also brought a major legal controversy. Spanish authorities accused him of concealing income from image rights and evading taxes between 2010 and 2014.In January 2019, Ronaldo accepted a 23-month suspended prison sentence and a financial penalty of approximately 18.8 million euros after admitting four tax offences. The tax evasion at the centre of the case was reported to involve around 5.7 million euros.Under Spanish law, prison sentences of less than two years are generally suspended for first-time offenders in cases of this nature. Ronaldo therefore did not serve time in prison.Kathryn Mayorga's sexual assault allegationIn 2018, a report brought renewed attention to an allegation made by Kathryn Mayorga, who claimed Ronaldo had sexually assaulted her in a Las Vegas hotel room in 2009.Ronaldo denied the allegation, maintaining that the encounter was consensual. Prosecutors in Las Vegas decided in 2019 that there was insufficient evidence to bring criminal charges.Mayorga subsequently filed a civil lawsuit seeking damages. In June 2022, a US judge dismissed the case with prejudice after finding serious misconduct by her lawyer, including the use of privileged communications. The dismissal was not a finding on the truth of the underlying allegation.Wayne Rooney's red card and the infamous World Cup winkOne of the most memorable controversies of Ronaldo's early career came during the 2006 FIFA World Cup quarter-final between Portugal and England.England forward Wayne Rooney was sent off after an incident involving Portugal defender Ricardo Carvalho, during which Rooney stamped on the defender. Ronaldo was seen appealing to the referee, while television cameras subsequently caught him winking towards the Portugal bench after Rooney's dismissal.The incident triggered outrage among English supporters, who accused Ronaldo of celebrating his Manchester United teammate's sending-off and influencing the referee. The episode intensified the scrutiny surrounding the young forward, although Ronaldo did not cause Rooney's red card. Obscene gesture towards Saudi supportersRonaldo faced disciplinary action in Saudi Arabia in February 2024 after Al-Nassr's 3-2 league victory over Al-Shabab.Videos circulating online showed the Portuguese forward cupping his ear and repeatedly moving his hand in front of his pelvic area in what appeared to be a response to chants of Lionel Messi's name from the stands.The gesture drew criticism and prompted a complaint. The Saudi Arabian Football Federation's disciplinary committee subsequently handed Ronaldo a one-match suspension and a fine of 10,000 Saudi riyals. He was also ordered to pay 20,000 riyals towards Al-Shabab's complaint costs.From a World Cup flashpoint and a turbulent Manchester United exit to legal battles and a bitter fallout with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, Ronaldo's career has rarely been short of headlines.
